ajad-p01.speaker: Utpaladeva, siddha voice (establishing the knower as non-inert)
ajad-p01.question: Can the inert (jaḍa) ground anything? What really distinguishes the existent (sat) from the nonexistent (asat)?
premises: v1: yathā sadasatām naiva viśeṣo 'sti nijātmani | jadājaḍānām apy evaṃ nāsty asāv iti niścayaḥ — just as there is no difference between real and unreal in their own self, so too — this is certain — there is no such difference between inert and non-inert.

v2: prakhyopākhyā ca sattā yad yad asattā viparyayaḥ | naitat svarūpaṃ spṛśati vastuno jñātṛgāmy adaḥ — appearing (prakhyā) and describing (upākhyā), existence and its opposite, non-existence — none of this touches a thing's essence; that essence faces the knower (jñātṛgāmi).

v3: prakhyopākhyāviṣayatāpy arthasyātmā na yujyate | parāpekṣitayā naikarūpatve sattvalaṅghanāt — a thing's self cannot be 'being-an-object-of-appearing' — that would depend on another, lack single form, overstep existence.

v4: mā bhūd viśeṣaḥ prakhyādibhāvābhāvau tataḥ punaḥ | siddhyaty eva viśeṣo 'tra tāvatā ca prayojanam — granted, let there be no difference; still, from presence/absence of appearing, a difference gets established — and that much serves the purpose.

v5: evam apy avabhāsānuṣaktā sattocitā bhavet | tadapekṣāṃ vinā bhāvābhāvayor aviśiṣṭatā — even so, existence would only be fitting as tied to appearing; without that reference, existent and nonexistent are indistinguishable.

v6: kathaṃ syād aviśeṣo 'tra yāvatārthakriyāṃ hi san | kuryān nānyas tathāpy artho nirviśeṣo nijātmani — but how could they be indistinguishable here, when the existent performs a function (arthakriyā) and the other does not? And yet the thing, in its own self, remains without distinction.

v7: evam arthakriyābhāsopādhisaṃbhedam āgataḥ | sann arthaḥ syāt svarūpeṇa nāsatas tu viśiṣyate — so the existent thing, having taken on the limiting condition of appearing-as-functional, would exist by its own essence — yet it is not distinguished from the nonexistent.

v8: tatrāpy arthakriyā siddhasattākārthe na varṇitā | samam evānayos tena pratiṣṭhā saṃvidāśrayā — but even there, function is not what is described in a thing whose existence is already established; the two are exactly on par — hence their grounding rests on consciousness.

v9: saṃvid apy aparāmarśarūpā cet tad asāv api | abhāvena jaḍenātha tulyaiva prāgvad ātmani — and if consciousness itself were of the form of non-reflection (aparāmarśa), then it too, in itself, would be exactly equal to the inert non-being, as before.
ajad-p01.inference: Every candidate ground (existence, function, appearing) collapses into consciousness-dependence; and consciousness without parāmarśa (self-reflection/vimarśa) is no better than the inert. Only self-reflective consciousness grounds. Self-luminosity (svaprakāśatvaṃ) is the determining factor between jaḍa and ajaḍa.
ajad-p01.conclusion: The inert grounds nothing; pratiṣṭhā rests on saṃvit alone, and only insofar as saṃvit is self-reflective. The knower must be conscious (ajaḍa), not inert (jaḍa).
ajad-p01.theorem: pratiṣṭhā = saṃvidāśrayā, and saṃvit must be aparāmarśa-free (self-reflective) to ground; svaprakāśatva is the jaḍa/ajaḍa divider.
unresolved_terms: mechanism by which parāmarśa confers grounding — deferred to vimarśa doctrine (p02, v. 15)
vṛtti by Harabhatta Shastri (not Utpaladeva); Lawrence 2009 critical edition
brief refutations of Vijñānavāda and Śāṅkara Vedānta; Śāṅkara refutation not developed in T1
two-level structure: pragmatic (limited knower) and ultimate/transcendental (unlimited knower)
ajad-p01.next_pressure: L2: no difference (v. 1) → appearing/describing (v. 2) → object-of-appearing (v. 3) → granted no difference (v. 4) → existence tied to appearing (v. 5) → objection: function (v. 6) → function conditioned (v. 7) → function not described (v. 8) → consciousness without reflection (v. 9). Key move: v. 9 — consciousness without parāmarśa is no better than the inert. Tone: scholastic (pramāṇa-style), not devotional. Two-level structure (pragmatic/ultimate) visible.

ajad-p02.speaker: Utpaladeva, continuing (siddha voice)
ajad-p02.question: How does consciousness ground another thing's manifestation? What is the 'I'?
premises: v10: saivaṃ bhūtātmanā svenāpy alabdhapariniṣṭhitiḥ | katham anyasya bhāvasya pratiṣṭhāspadatām iyāt — if it has not, by its own self-nature, attained final grounding, how could it become the ground of establishment for another existent?

v11: idam ity ucitaḥ saṃvit prakāśe 'nyasya vastunaḥ | pratiṣṭhātmakatāṃ gacched aham ity ātmanā punaḥ — consciousness, fitly manifesting as 'this' (idam), would attain the nature of grounding another thing's manifestation — and again, by itself, as 'I' (aham).

v12: vyatireketarābhyām hi niścayo 'nyajaḍātmanoḥ | vyavasthitiḥ pratiṣṭhā ca siddhir nirvṛttir ucyate — for certainty — by exclusion (vyatireka) and by inclusion (itara) alike — is called the fixed order, the foundation, the attainment, the completion of the other inert selves.

v13: evam ātmany asatkalpāḥ prakāśasyaiva santy amī | jaḍāḥ prakāśa evāsti svātmanaḥ svaparātmabhiḥ — so these inert things, almost unreal in themselves, exist only as light's own; light alone exists — of one's own self, through selves own and other.

v14: na caivānubhavo 'py asti bhinnābhinnaviniścayam | muktvānvayasya prakāśasya vimarśarahitātmanaḥ — and there is no experience apart from the certainty of the distinct and the indistinct, apart from the connected light whose self is without reflection.

v15: idam ity asya vicchinnnavimarśasya kṛtārthatā | yā svasvarūpe viśrāntir vimarśaḥ so 'ham ity ayam — of this 'this'-consciousness whose reflection is cut off, the fulfillment is rest in its own essence; that reflection — 'I am this' — is just this.

v16: dvidhā sa eṣa evātmā mito 'parimitas tathā | prāṇādinā niruddho 'ṇuḥ paramātmā tv akhaṇḍitaḥ — this same self is twofold: measured and unmeasured — confined by breath and the rest, it is the atom (aṇu); as supreme self, it is undivided.

v17: ubhayo 'py eṣa paryantabhūmiḥ sarvārthasaṃvidām | eka evānusandhānād ato 'nyo nopapadyate — of both, this one alone is the ultimate ground of all object-consciousnesses; it is one alone through continuity (anusaṃdhāna) — so no other is possible.

v18: na cāpy avyatirekātma-vimarśātmany ahaṃvidi | bhāti paryantavartinyāṃ bhāsanād adhikaṃ jaḍam — in the I-consciousness whose self is reflection of non-separation, dwelling at the limit, nothing more inert than manifestation appears.
ajad-p02.inference: Grounding runs through the idam/aham polarity resolved in continuity; exclusion and inclusion together yield the fourfold certainty (vyavasthiti/pratiṣṭhā/siddhi/nirvṛtti); the limited and unlimited self are one continuum. The inert selves derive their entire order from the self-reflective 'I.' The two-level structure: pragmatic (limited knower, aṇu) and ultimate/transcendental (unlimited knower, paramātman).
ajad-p02.conclusion: The self — twofold yet one through anusaṃdhāna — is the sole ground; the inert selves derive their entire order (vyavasthiti through nirvṛtti) from it. No other ground is possible.
ajad-p02.theorem: Ground = aham (self-reflective 'I') via idam/aham polarity resolved in anusaṃdhāna; self is twofold (mīta/aparimita) but one.
unresolved_terms: mechanism by which parāmarśa confers grounding — deferred to vimarśa doctrine (v. 15)
vṛtti by Harabhatta Shastri; Lawrence 2009 critical edition
brief refutations of Vijñānavāda and Śāṅkara Vedānta; Śāṅkara refutation not developed in T1
ajad-p02.next_pressure: L2: what is ungrounded cannot ground (v. 10) → idam and aham (v. 11) → fourfold certainty (v. 12) → inert things exist only as light's own (v. 13) → no experience without certainty (v. 14) → 'I am this' (v. 15) → twofold self (v. 16) → one through continuity (v. 17) → end-residing I (v. 18). Key: v. 15 ('I am this' is the reflection itself) and v. 17 (two are one through continuity; no other ground). Tone: scholastic. Two-level structure (pragmatic/ultimate) visible.

ajad-p03.speaker: Utpaladeva, concluding (siddha voice)
ajad-p03.question: Are breath, body, the eightfold city the knower? What is Māyā? What is the world?
premises: v19: na siddho 'prathanād eva jñānādisamavāyy api | tat prāṇādi prameyaṃ syān na pramātānyato bhramāt — breath etc., though joined with knowledge, are not established by non-manifestation; they are objects (prameya), not the knower — else delusion.

v20: yady apy arthasthitiḥ prāṇapuryaṣṭakaniyantrite | jīve niruddhā tatrāpi paramātmani sā sthitā — though things stand confined in the living being (breath, eightfold city), even there they abide in the supreme self.

v21: tadātmanaiva tasya syāt kathaṃ prāṇena yantraṇā | sādhitā pratyabhijñāyām akhyāter jīvatā param — restraint by breath cannot establish that self-nature; in recognition (pratyabhijñā), the living being is supreme over non-manifestation.

v22: nārthavyavasthā prāṇādāv ahaṃbhāvanirodhataḥ | prakāśasyātmaviśrāntir ahaṃbhāvo hi kīrtitaḥ — the ordering of things is not in breath etc. via I-restraint; rest of manifestation in itself is proclaimed as I-ness.

v23: uktā saiva ca viśrāntiḥ sarvāpekṣānirodhataḥ | svātantryam atha kartṛtvaṃ mukhyam īśvaratāpi ca — that rest — restraint of all dependence — is autonomy (svātantrya), principal authorship (kartṛtva), lordship (īśvaratā).

v24: māyābhidās tacchakter eva cānyāprasiddhitaḥ | tadakhyātimayaṃ hy etaj jagannirmātṛteśitā — named Māyā, it is of his power alone (no other established); the world-maker's lordship consists of non-manifestation (akhyāti).

v25: ekaiva cānusaṃdhānāt sā proktā sarvasaṃvidām | svasaṃvedanaparyāyamātṛtattvam anādi tat — proclaimed one alone through continuity: the mother-principle (mātṛtattva) of all consciousnesses, equivalent to self-experience, beginningless.

v26: bhāvavyavasthā yan niṣṭhā tasyāhaṃbhāvabhāginaḥ | vyāpitvam anusaṃdhānaṃ taj jaḍasya na yujyate — the final ground of things' ordering — pervasion and continuity partaking in I-ness — does not fit the inert.

v27: tato bhede tu bhāsasya ghaṭate bhāsamānatā | tenoktam pratyabhijñāyāṃ tadadvayamayaṃ jagat — hence in difference, manifestation's appearing holds; therefore: this world consists of that non-dual (tadadvayamayaṃ jagat).
ajad-p03.inference: Prāṇa/body are prameya (objects of knowledge), not pramātṛ (knower). The knower is the resting, autonomous I (svātantrya, kartṛtva, īśvaratā). Māyā is Śiva's own power (śakti), the power of non-manifestation (akhyāti) — not an independent principle. One beginningless mother-principle (mātṛtattva), self-experience itself, proclaimed through continuity. Pervasion (vyāpitva) and continuity (anusaṃdhāna) belong only to what partakes in I-ness (ahaṃbhāva); the inert cannot have them. The world proclaimed in recognition is non-dual (tadadvayamayaṃ jagat). Two-level structure: pragmatic (limited knower, aṇu) and ultimate/transcendental (unlimited knower, paramātman).
ajad-p03.conclusion: One beginningless mother-principle, self-experience itself; the world proclaimed in recognition is non-dual (tadadvayamayaṃ jagat). The unlimited knower (paramātman) is the only knower. This is the APS's conclusion.
ajad-p03.theorem: mātṛtattva = svasaṃvedana (self-experience), anādi; Māyā = Śiva's śakti (akhyāti); jagat = tadadvayamayaṃ (non-dual in recognition).
unresolved_terms: mechanism by which parāmarśa confers grounding — deferred to vimarśa doctrine (p02, v. 15)

ajad-p03.next_pressure: L2: breath etc. are not established (v. 19) → abiding in the supreme (v. 20) → restraint by breath (v. 21) → ordering is not in breath (v. 22) → that rest is autonomy (v. 23) → Māyā is his power (v. 24) → one mother-principle (v. 25) → pervasion belongs to I-ness (v. 26) → the world is non-dual (v. 27).
